public_rationale: NVIDIA's rounded disclosures are consistent with hyperscalers contributing more than half of revenue. Reporting about Amazon also gives a concrete example of hardware arriving before power is available, although outside the selected quarter. Neither establishes repeated stockpiling across hyperscalers or that stockpiling alone constrained supply. Those central assertions remain unproved.
limitations: The revenue calculation uses rounded company figures.
Purchase orders, delivered inventory and operational GPUs are different measures.
The cited Amazon account is secondary reporting about a later period.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: It appears that hyperscalers, which make up more than 50% of NVIDIA's revenue, are willing quarter after quarter to buy GPUs in advance, hoarding tens of billions of dollars to 'secure supply' that is constrained only because of the hyperscalers themselves.

statement.excerpt: Yet it appears that hyperscalers — which make up more than 50% of its revenue — are willing to do so, quarter after quarter, hoarding tens of billions of dollars to “secure supply” that is only constrained because of the hyperscalers themselves.

from_speaker: hoarding tens of billions of dollars
only constrained because of the hyperscalers themselves
our_interpretation: Read as three linked assertions: hyperscalers supply over half of NVIDIA's total revenue; they repeatedly accumulate substantial GPU purchases before deployment; their accumulation alone creates the supply constraint.
Read 'hoarding tens of billions of dollars' as holding purchased hardware worth that amount, rather than holding cash.
Use NVIDIA's latest completed fiscal quarter before publication for the revenue share: the quarter ended July 26, 2026. Repeated purchasing requires evidence from preceding quarters as well.
'It appears' expresses uncertainty, rather than an antecedent that must occur.
The supplied passage does not identify the accounting basis or source of the revenue percentage. Do not silently assign one.
criteria.support_condition: Matching revenue disclosures establish the greater-than-50% share, purchase and deployment records establish repeated accumulation worth tens of billions, and causal evidence establishes that this accumulation alone constrained supply.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Matching records disprove a specified component, or causal evidence establishes a material supply constraint that would remain without hyperscaler stockpiling.

evidence.explanation: The transcript also reports rounded total quarterly revenue of $96 billion, implying approximately 51% from hyperscale customers. This is consistent with the percentage component, but does not establish stockpiling or causation; the claim's accounting basis remains unspecified.

This secondary report describes hardware arriving ahead of available power. It concerns one buyer after the target quarter, and the underlying emails were not available for inspection; it cannot establish repeated industry-wide accumulation or sole causation.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Matched quarterly purchaser inventories and deployment dates, a specified revenue accounting basis, and evidence separating stockpiling's effect from independent supply bottlenecks.
